method: Whole-file manual reading of update, registry and clipboard managers; exact-commit downloads matched pinned Git blob IDs. No updates, registry writes or clipboard access executed.
findings: Update asset selection uses first matching underscore-split filename with runtime StartsWith and architecture equality. Prefix matching is not exact runtime validation; unknown architectures default x64. URL/hash/signature validation not present in this wrapper; dependency behavior not reviewed here.

Update metadata parse errors are Debug logged, null fields can fail parsing, and missing matching asset yields null DownloadURL. Helper.GetIcon null-forgiven in static initialization can fail earlier. No actual update request executed.

Registry helper opens existing HKCU subkeys rather than creating missing keys; null keys silently skip writes. Startup Run value stores executable path directly without quoting; actual Windows launch handling not tested. Run and StartupApproved edits are separate nontransactional writes.

Clipboard writes empty existing contents before allocation/publication succeeds, so failures can lose prior data. SetClipboardData return ignored; allocation is not freed on rejected publication. No success/failure result exposed.

Clipboard GlobalLock/Unlock is not protected by inner finally around allocation/copy, so exceptions can skip unlock. GlobalSize declared uint and cast to int for copying lacks explicit admission bounds. Source-level interop concerns, no runtime memory corruption investigated.

Clipboard generic backup skips bitmap/enhanced metafile but treats all other formats as movable-memory bytes; format-specific handle semantics and delayed rendering not qualified. Reads can return partial dictionary after exception.

CloseClipboard called in finally even if OpenClipboard failed; empty strings/partial data conflate unavailable clipboard and actual empty contents. These patterns are unsuitable as reliable scanner evidence transport.
limits: No Windows API execution, updater dependency audit, clipboard fault injection or original tests. No foreign production code adopted.
